newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba says Clinton hostage of U.S. Congress.
newsitem.headline: Cuba says Clinton hostage of U.S. Congress.

text.p: In a biting attack on legislative proposals to further tighten the U.S. embargo on Cuba, Cuban Foreign Minister Roberto Robaina has charged that President Bill Clinton and the executive branch have given up their constitutional prerogatives to Congress.

"The American Congress has succeeded in snatching away the constitutional rights of the White House ... converting it to a hostage of Congress," Robaina said in an exclusive interview carried in Sunday's Juventud Rebelde.
Robaina was referring to a series of Cuba-related proposals that will be voted on in the U.S. House of Representatives this week as part of an omnibus foreign policy reform law (HR 1486).
The proposals were introduced by a representative from Florida, Ileana Ros Lehtinen, who represents the most hardline sectors of the Cuban-American community.

The proposals strengthen the U.S embargo on trade with Cuba and places the president's application of the law under tighter congressional scrutiny, making it more difficult for him to manoeuvre within the framework of the law and interpret it more liberally.

Title III of the Helms-Burton law allows U.S citizens to sue foreign enterprises in federal courts for using properties that were seized from them under Cuba's nationalisation laws in the early 1960s. This includes those citizens that were Cuban nationals at the time their property was confiscated.
President Clinton has already used his right to postpone the suits against foreign enterprises twice, following angry denunciations of the law by Canada, Mexico and members of the European Community.

Title IV requires the U.S. government to prohibit the officials of those companies and their families from entering the United States. So far, the Department of Justice has applied the ban to only two companies.

Robaina said that the new proposals to be brought before the full House of Representatives this week will increase Washington's tensions with its allies who oppose the Helms- Burton law on the grounds that it imposes U.S. policy "extraterritorially" on them.

Robaina said that the real intention of the Helms-Burton law "is to sow terror, chaos, hunger and sicknesses in our country and among our people; to destroy our nation, its independence and sovereignty, and to re-establish neocolonial control".
